summary: Floirac is a Bordeaux Métropole commune on the right bank where parking policy is set mostly by the Métropole, with the town managing one small blue-zone car park in the centre-bourg (27 places, 90 free minutes on weekdays). The Bordeaux low-emission zone has covered the area inside the ring road since January 2025, and two Floirac park-and-ride sites, Arena and Dravemont, are among the 11 that unclassified vehicles may still reach. TBM lists Dravemont as a 46-space tram A park-and-ride, and Metpark, a public body, runs the roughly 1,000-place Arkéa Arena car park. The town steers concert-goers to park-and-rides and the Arena shuttle, and the national database shows at least 29 public charge points at Floirac addresses, including six 180 kW points on rue de la Gabarre. No town-wide paid on-street or resident parking scheme turned up in the sources read.

items.text: Since 1 January 2025 Bordeaux Métropole's low-emission zone (ZFE) covers everything inside the ring road, 24/7, and a Crit'Air sticker is required. Only unclassified vehicles (for example petrol or diesel cars registered before 1 January 1997) are barred from driving or parking inside; the page was last updated on 13 January 2026.
items.source_title: ZFE (Zone à Faibles Émissions) : ce qu'il faut savoir

items.text: Unclassified vehicles may still reach 11 park-and-ride sites inside the ring road by dedicated access roads; two of them are in Floirac, Parc Relais Arena and Parc Relais Dravemont. The Métropole says 8,000 Gironde households (3.7%) own an unclassified vehicle.
items.source_title: ZFE (Zone à Faibles Émissions) : ce qu'il faut savoir

items.text: The town's centre-bourg car park on rue Jules Guesde (next to the maison des combattants) is a blue zone with 27 places, a 90-minute free stay Monday to Friday, 3 drop-off places, 1 disabled place and 2 electric charging points. Automatic detection sensors linked to the municipal police monitor the time limit. The same page gives the blue-zone hours both as 8am-7pm and as 8.30am-7pm.
items.source_title: Parking du centre bourg : stationnez malin

items.text: On public roads in Floirac, municipal and national police handle abusive parking; under the Highway Code a vehicle left in one spot for more than 7 days, or less where a local order sets it, counts as abusive and can be impounded. On private land only the national police can act.
Floirac became a '30 km/h town' in 2023 after neighbourhood-council consultation in spring 2022. Only the quais de la Souys and part of avenue François Mitterrand stay at 50 km/h.

For Arkéa Arena events the town urges spectators to use public transport, bike or car-sharing, and to park at TBM park-and-ride sites linked to the special Arena shuttle. Anti-parking bollards have been installed and the municipal police check parking after shows, with regular fines and impoundments for vehicles blocking pavements, bus stops or business entrances.
items.source_title: Stationnement les soirs de concert à l'Arena

items.text: The Arena's own multi-storey car park is run by Metpark and has close to 1,000 places, including more than 20 for motorised two-wheelers; a space can be bought together with a show ticket. The town also lists a 20-place bike-share station and more than 500 bike hoops (1,000 places) near the hall.
items.source_title: Stationnement les soirs de concert à l'Arena

items.text: The Arkéa Arena 2026 accessibility guide also gives 'close to 1,000' places for the Metpark car park, 22 of them for reduced-mobility visitors who can book with their tickets up to 48 hours before an event. It directs drivers to ring-road exit 22b ('Bas Floirac Arena'); the PDF is undated and was read on 21 October 2026.

Metpark describes itself as a public industrial and commercial body (EPIC) for Bordeaux and its metropolis, governed by a board of 11 Métropole elected members. Its page says it plans to install 1,500 charge points in 26 car parks by 2026 under a public concession, and to invest over 25 million euros in renovating 4 car parks by 2026; the page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026.

TBM's English park-and-ride list (undated, read on 21 October 2026) shows Dravemont, opposite the Dravemont shopping centre in Floirac, as 'TBM season ticket holders only' with 46 spaces, 4 disabled spaces and 14 bicycle spaces, on the tram A list. It does not list a Floirac Arena park-and-ride.
items.source_title: Opening times, maps and list of Parcs-Relais

items.text: TBM says its park-and-rides open when trams run: 5am-1am on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Sunday and holidays, and 5am-2am on Thursday to Saturday. Using one outside tram hours can bring a EUR 15 per day fine; the page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: Opening times, maps and list of Parcs-Relais

items.text: TBM's short-stay park-and-ride tickets cost EUR 12 (2 days), 15 (3 days), 20 (4 days) and 25 (5 days), each including one round trip on the network. Floirac Dravemont is among 11 of the 28 sites offering them, which sits oddly with the same site's season-ticket-only listing; the page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026.

A September 2024 TBM Arena leaflet gives the park-and-ride ticket as EUR 4.50 (prices of 1 July 2024): parking plus one return trip the same day, whatever the number of people in the car, up to 7. It is sold only at the machines of the tram station by the park, and the leaflet says 28 park-and-ride sites serve the metropolis.
items.source_title: Aller à l'Arkéa Arena (TBM leaflet, September 2024)

items.text: On show days TBM runs an Arena shuttle from Stalingrad and Gare Saint-Jean, from 2 hours before the event to 1 hour after, every 5 to 10 minutes. The leaflet also lists buses 6, 16, 25 and 28 serving the Arena, with line 6 running to Floirac Dravemont.
items.source_title: Aller à l'Arkéa Arena (TBM leaflet, September 2024)

items.text: The national charge-point database (file of 19 October 2026) lists at least 9 charge-point stations with 29 points at Floirac addresses. These include 6 x 180 kW IZIVIA points on rue de la Gabarre (in service since 7 November 2024) and a 7-point EVzen site on chemin de Vimeney with six 180 kW points.

The same database lists Bordeaux Métropole-developed Freshmile points in Floirac on rue Jules Guesde and rue Coluche (public car parks, 24 and 22 kW) and on avenue Mitterrand and rue Dominique Ingres (on street, 7.4 to 22 kW). A 4-point 22 kW Partage Ma Borne site sits at the Greet hotel beside the Arena (since 2 November 2022).

gaps: https://www.bordeaux-metropole.fr/en-voiture/parcs-stationnement and https://www.bordeaux-metropole.fr/en-voiture/recharger-mon-vehicule-electrique returned 403, so the Métropole's own car park and charging pages were not read.

https://www.infotbm.com/en/titles-and-prices/park-and-ride-tickets and https://www.infotbm.com/fr/actualites/des-nouveautes-dans-les-parcs-relais.html returned 403, so the current park-and-ride fare and any reduced-fare list for Dravemont are unverified; the only fare read is the July 2024 EUR 4.50 from a leaflet.

https://www.infotbm.com/fr/parc-relais (French park-and-ride list, which may hold live availability) returned an empty page; the undated English list gives Dravemont as season-ticket-only, which conflicts with its place on the short-stay list.

https://www.lejournaldesentreprises.com/article/bordeaux-metropole-attribue-la-construction-du-futur-pont-jean-jacques-bosc-92574 returned a bot-check (429). No usable source on the Pont Jean-Jacques Bosc opening or its parking effects was read, so it is not covered.

No Floirac council decision on paid or resident on-street parking was found, and the Floirac Arena park-and-ride (about 200 places per one search result) was not confirmed by any page read. Sud Ouest and actu.fr could not be searched (domains not accessible to the search tool), and the Bordeaux Métropole ZFE page gives no later calendar for stricter Crit'Air phases.
Charge-point counts come from the national database filtered on Floirac address text, so stations with missing address data may be absent and some entries lack a commissioning date.
